classification.difficultyReason: Combine unit conversion, Pythagoras and two distance–speed relationships to form a time model.

content.prompt:
Taylor swims from point $A$ to point $B$ across a 500 m wide river, then walks along the river to point $C$. The distance along the river is 7 km. If she swims at $5\text{ km h}^{-1}$ and walks at $4\text{ km h}^{-1}$, show that the time taken to reach point $C$ is given by
$$t=\frac{\sqrt{x^2+0.25}}{5}+\frac{7-x}{4}.$$

spec.description: Two horizontal riverbanks, with A on the lower bank, a dashed perpendicular to the upper bank, B to the right of its foot and C farther right. AB is the diagonal swimming route. The upper-bank distance from the foot to B is x, and the dimension from the foot to C is 7 km. Schematic proportions carry no additional measurements.
spec.mathematics: AB is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with perpendicular distances 0.5 km and x km; BC has length 7−x km.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram content is permanently visible; no solution values are added.

answer.worked:
The river is 500 m, or 0.5 km, wide.

Distance $AB$, by Pythagoras:
$$\begin{align*}d_{AB}&=\sqrt{x^2+0.5^2}\\d_{AB}&=\sqrt{x^2+0.25}\text{ km}.\end{align*}$$
Using $\text{time}=\dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}}$,
$$t_{AB}=\frac{\sqrt{x^2+0.25}}{5}\text{ hours}.$$
Distance $BC$:
$$d_{BC}=7-x\text{ km}.$$
Hence
$$t_{BC}=\frac{7-x}{4}\text{ hours}.$$
So the total time taken is
$$\begin{align*}t&=t_{AB}+t_{BC}\\t&=\frac{\sqrt{x^2+0.25}}{5}+\frac{7-x}{4}\text{ hours}.\end{align*}$$
